question: Does backing off singleton pair features improve recovery or decision coverage relative to neutral-unknown v109, with scorer/counts fixed?
scope: Exposed supervised development comparison on same v107 rows/splits/roles; not fresh confirmation, no Voynich access, no clustering or automatic role count run.
structural_fact: v109 already includes four component word-at-position features plus two pair features; unknown pairs are neutral. Literal unseen-pair fallback without duplicating word evidence is mathematically identical to baseline.

rule.rare: A pair is rare if its pooled binary-role training occurrence count is exactly1. Repeated support begins at2; this is a single preregistered singleton-removal rule, not a tuned threshold grid.
rule.baseline: Exactly v109 repaired scorer, fitted counts, vocabulary, denominators, unigrams, priors and abstention tolerance.
rule.backoff: Send all four original component features plus only pair features with pooled training count>=2 to the unmodified v109 repaired score function. Singleton pair contributes no extra evidence; its component features remain present exactly once. Unknown pairs are already neutral. Counts/vocabulary/denominators remain baseline-fitted: this is activation-only backoff, not a refit that changes unrelated word scores.
rule.invariants: No duplicate component features, broader context, position sharing, new word forms, changed alpha or key fitting. All originally recognized component words stay active. Zero-evidence cases cannot gain support; decision coverage may still change through ties. Pair evidence of either sign may be lost; retain harms.
rule.training_only: Pair activation is derived from training counts pooled across roles. Test frequencies and gold labels cannot set thresholds or activation.

evaluation.panels: All eight prior panels; four prior adequately supported panels form equal-weight primary development summary, others remain descriptive.
evaluation.metrics: Reuse v109 balanced correct-credit (.5 for abstention), strict balanced recall (abstentions misses), coverage, balanced log loss and two-class Brier. Compare on all cases and fixed v109 evidence-bearing subset. Record every gained/lost prediction and abstention.
evaluation.uncertainty: 2000 paired whole-test-block bootstrap draws per panel with v109 unchanged bootstrap function; descriptive95% intervals only. No training-fit uncertainty or fresh-data inference.
evaluation.controls: Same199 context-column within-block shuffles and199 training-label within-block shuffles per panel, fitting one shared count model for baseline/backoff in each trial. Record both metrics and paired deltas, recompute training pair frequencies per control. Seeds1101000/1102000 and bootstrap1103000. Retain all3184control trials. Structured nuisance nulls, not automatic method qualification.
evaluation.criterion: Answer by paired recovery/coverage/score changes; no claim from a favorable subset, new threshold or tie policy. Expected-credit gain with worse strict recall/coverage must be explicit. No qualification promotion.

fixtures: Literal unknown-pair fallback is score-identical to baseline.
Every component feature appears once after backoff.
Singleton pair is suppressed; repeated pair is retained.
Known-only score differences equal exactly the removed singleton terms.
Pair support comes only from baseline training counts.
A genuinely predictive singleton may be harmed; backoff is not assumed beneficial.
limits: Only one fixed activation rule is tested. A negative result does not reject all smoothing or pair interpolation. v107/v109 are exposed development data and no independent-source claim is available.
